findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the exact predicate the fold uses to choose union vs refuse for an unrelated-history head (which reference state it inspects, and why it differs from sync's local-HEAD _carries_ticket_events gate given all heads are same-ref), so both the losslessness claim in step 4 and the refuse oracle in AC line 9 are simultaneously satisfiable.

AC 9: 'except its refuse path (genuinely unrelated head while the local store carries events) aborts, deletes nothing remotely, and surfaces fsck-recover. Verified by an unrelated-history oracle.'

sync.py:144-153 _do_reconverge gates the refuse on _carries_ticket_events(tracker) of the LOCAL HEAD; after the first fold merge HEAD carries events, so that predicate cannot be reused verbatim to select among same-ref heads
findings.finding: The plan's unrelated-history handling is internally inconsistent and leaves the refuse-vs-union decision predicate unspecified: it claims every fetched head is a tip of the same configured ref (hence always losslessly unionable, so the refuse path 'only fires on a genuinely unrelated head'), yet AC line 9 requires an oracle proving the refuse path DOES fire (aborts, deletes nothing, surfaces fsck-recover). The plan never states how the fold distinguishes a same-ref unrelated head (must union) from a 'genuinely unrelated head while the local store carries events' (must refuse). Sync's analogous gate (_carries_ticket_events at sync.py:80/144) keys off the LOCAL HEAD carrying events — but after the first merge HEAD is the local store and always carries events, so mechanically reusing that gate would refuse the very same-ref heads the plan says to union. Without a defined predicate the implementer cannot both make the fold lossless AND satisfy the refuse oracle.

scenarios: Two bundles for the same ref that share no merge-base (e.g. a re-init on one clone) — the fold must decide union vs refuse but the plan gives no operative rule

Implementer copies sync's _carries_ticket_events gate and every unrelated head after the first merge is refused, defeating losslessness; or omits it and the refuse oracle (AC 9) can never be exercised

findings.finding: The plan's contended-lock recovery narrative is internally inconsistent: it says a doctor that finds the S3 lock held should 'back off and let the normal retry re-detect', but it also specifies a single `healed_once` guard that trips on ANY heal invocation -- including a no-op return when the lock was unavailable. A doctor that loses the S3 lock therefore consumes its one heal attempt without collapsing the bundles; the retried push still hits the multi-bundle state, `healed_once` blocks re-invocation, and the push falls through to the non-FF/terminal classification instead of re-healing. The loser of a repair storm never converges on that push (it must wait for a whole new push cycle).
findings.location: Approach — Heal algorithm step 1 (lock back-off) vs. Detection paragraph (`healed_once` guard)
findings.suggested_fix: Have `heal_multi_bundle` distinguish 'locked/no-op' from 'healed' in its return, and in `push_tickets_branch` set `healed_once=True` only on an effective heal; for a 'locked' outcome, apply a bounded backoff-and-re-detect (small attempt cap) so the loser re-enters detection after the winner converges.
